Select a training sample above, then capture it.What the network computesEach layer computes z=Wa+b, then an activation. Hidden activations allow nonlinear boundaries. With no hidden layer this is logistic regression, so it cannot solve XOR. Binary cross entropy and a sigmoid output give the output delta p−y. Hidden deltas use the chain rule: transpose weights times the next delta, multiplied by the activation derivative. Full-batch gradients are averaged across training examples before weights and biases are updated.ReLU has derivative 0 at and below zero by convention. Initialization matters; small networks can reach local solutions. This visualizer trains tiny two-feature models, not large deep-learning tasks. The held-out split contains 23 examples and not used in gradient updates.

sections.text: Optimize one known scalar quadratic and inspect every real parameter update.

sections.title: How It Works
sections.text: Differentiate f(w)=(w−3)² to obtain 2(w−3).Multiply the derivative by the selected positive rate.Subtract that displacement and record the newly computed loss.

sections.title: Dataset
sections.text: This is an analytic objective, not a fitted dataset. The initial position is −3 and the exact optimum is w=3. No train/test metric is appropriate for this demonstration.

sections.title: Practical Applications
sections.text: Gradient descent trains differentiable models by reducing an objective. This exactly solvable quadratic isolates stability; it does not demonstrate stochasticity, nonconvex optimization or neural generalization. Use the optimizer workbench for multidimensional objectives.
